slot.brief: Given a two-way/percentage breakdown, compute a conditional probability of one event given the other; direct formula with the joint probability.

stem: In a factory, $70\%$ of the workers are skilled and the rest are unskilled. Among skilled workers, $20\%$ are women; among unskilled workers, $40\%$ are women. If a randomly chosen worker is found to be a woman, the probability that she is skilled is:
working:
Let total workers = 100. Skilled = 70, Unskilled = 30.
Women skilled = 0.20 × 70 = 14, Women unskilled = 0.40 × 30 = 12.
Total women = 14 + 12 = 26.
Required probability = 14/26 = 7/13.

Independent check: P(\text{skilled and woman})=0.7(0.2)=0.14; P(\text{woman})=0.14+0.3(0.4)=0.26. Thus P(\text{skilled}\mid\text{woman})=0.14/0.26=7/13.
solution:
Let the total number of workers be $100$. Then skilled women $=70(0.20)=14$, and unskilled women $=30(0.40)=12$.
$$P(\text{skilled}\mid\text{woman})=\frac{14}{14+12}=\boxed{\frac{7}{13}}$$
